Looking at the jagged edges: each piece's top and right edges have a single "bump–notch" pattern (either notch-then-bump or bump-then-notch), except piece B, whose top edge has a double wave (two bumps and two notches).

When four pieces assemble into the square, every jagged edge must interlock with exactly one jagged edge of a neighboring piece: a bump on one side must fit a notch on the other. The single bump–notch edges of A, C, D, and E can be paired up (using rotations/flips): e.g., A's top with C's right, A's right with E's top, C's top with D's right, E's right with D's top.

Piece B's doubly-wavy top edge, however, has no complementary edge among the other pieces (no other piece has a matching double wave), so B can never fit into the square.
